text: Rule ID: S_3.2.1 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CRD (all 3 documents) Parameter field: submission_timestamp Operator: <= Limit value: event_handbook_deadline Units: date FSG reference: S 3.2.1, p.112 Deterministic: True Rule text: Three CRD must be submitted to the competition website by the deadline specified in the Event Handbook. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary: submitted by deadline or not. Machine-checkable given a deadline and a submission timestamp.

Rule ID: S_3.3.1 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CRD package Parameter field: document_set_present Operator: == Limit value: {BOM_CCBOM, SupportingMaterialFile_pdf, CostEmissionsExplanationFile_pdf} Units: set_membership FSG reference: S 3.3.1, p.113 Deterministic: True Rule text: The CRD consist of: the BOM (incl. CCBOM), the Supporting Material File (PDF), and the Cost and Emissions Explanation File (PDF). Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary checklist of required documents - either all three exist or they don't.

Rule ID: S_3.3.6 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CRD (all 3 documents) Parameter field: presented_vs_submitted_hash Operator: == Limit value: identical Units: boolean FSG reference: S 3.3.6, p.113 Deterministic: True Rule text: The presented CRD must be identical to the submitted versions, otherwise 0 points will be scored for BOM Discussion. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary comparison (file diff / hash match) between submitted and presented versions. Notes: 0 points for BOM Discussion if mismatched

Rule ID: S_3.4.1 Source type: hard Affected part/category: BOM - all parts Parameter field: sort_order Operator: == Limit value: sorted Units: boolean FSG reference: S 3.4.1, p.114 Deterministic: True Rule text: The BOM is a sorted list of all vehicle parts. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Structural/formatting requirement - checkable by verifying sort order and completeness against a parts list.

Rule ID: S_3.4.3 Source type: engineering Affected part/category: BOM - all parts Parameter field: part_presence_vs_physical_vehicle Operator: == Limit value: complete_match Units: boolean FSG reference: S 3.4.3, p.114 Deterministic: False Rule text: The BOM must list all parts fitted to the prototype vehicle at any time during the event. Classification: engineering-soundness Classification rationale: Requires comparing the physical vehicle to the BOM - objectively verifiable in principle (a judge inspects the car) but not purely machine-checkable from the BOM file alone. Notes: Requires physical vehicle inspection by judge - not machine-checkable from BOM file alone

Rule ID: S_3.4.5 Source type: interpretive Affected part/category: BOM - fastener/part boundary Parameter field: item_classification Operator: in Limit value: {part, fastener} Units: category FSG reference: S 3.4.5, p.114 Deterministic: False Rule text: Fasteners (e.g. DIN-931 hexagon screws, glue, zip ties, tape used for mounting) are separate from parts and should not be listed as parts. Tape for edge protection or safety wire ARE considered parts. Classification: interpretive Classification rationale: Requires judgement to classify borderline items (e.g. is a specific tape 'for mounting' or 'for edge protection'?) - the rule itself provides examples rather than a strict test, implying edge cases need human judgement. Notes: Borderline cases (e.g. tape type) require human judgement

Rule ID: S_3.4.6 Source type: hard Affected part/category: BOM - fasteners Parameter field: self_manufactured Operator: == Limit value: true -> classify_as_part Units: boolean FSG reference: S 3.4.6, p.114 Deterministic: True Rule text: A self-manufactured fastener is considered a part. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary rule with a clear test: self-manufactured (yes/no) determines classification (part vs fastener).

Rule ID: S_3.4.7 Source type: hard Affected part/category: BOM - all parts Parameter field: system_assignment Operator: in Limit value: {Autonomous System, Brake System, Chassis and Body, Drivetrain, Engine and Tractive System, Grounded Low Voltage System, Miscellaneous Fit and Finish, Steering System, Suspension System, Wheels Wheel Bearings and Tires} Units: enum FSG reference: S 3.4.7, p.114 Deterministic: True Rule text: The BOM must be broken down into 10 specified systems (Autonomous System, Brake System, Chassis and Body, Drivetrain, Engine and Tractive System, Grounded Low Voltage System, Miscellaneous Fit and Finish, Steering System, Suspension System, Wheels/Bearings/Tires). Classification: hard Classification rationale: Fixed enumerated list - each part's system assignment can be validated against this closed set.

Rule ID: S_3.4.8 Source type: interpretive Affected part/category: BOM - all parts Parameter field: part_name_clarity Operator: subjective_review Limit value: N/A Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.4.8, p.114 Deterministic: False Rule text: The chosen part name must clearly describe what is included (e.g. a spring should not be called 'damper'). Classification: interpretive Classification rationale: Naming clarity/accuracy is a judgement call, not machine-checkable without a part-name-to-function ontology (which doesn't exist). Notes: No ontology exists to machine-check name accuracy

Rule ID: S_3.4.9 Source type: hard Affected part/category: BOM - all parts Parameter field: unit_system Operator: in Limit value: {mm, kg, m3, EUR, ...metric_units} Units: unit_type FSG reference: S 3.4.9, p.114 Deterministic: True Rule text: Only metric units must be used within the BOM. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary, pattern-matchable: unit strings can be checked against a metric-units whitelist. Notes: Pattern-matchable against a metric-units whitelist

Rule ID: S_3.5.2 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM Parameter field: system_covered Operator: includes Limit value: Engine and Tractive System Units: system_name FSG reference: S 3.5.2, p.115 Deterministic: True Rule text: For 2026, a CCBOM for the Engine and Tractive System must be submitted. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary presence check for a specific required system's CCBOM section.

Rule ID: S_3.5.3 Source type: engineering Affected part/category: CCBOM - all parts Parameter field: cost_realism Operator: subjective_review Limit value: N/A Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.5.3, p.115 Deterministic: False Rule text: The CCBOM must include: actual manufacturing processes used, tooling, actual costs (materials/fabrication/bought parts/assembly), and carbon footprint in CO2e per part/process. Classification: engineering-soundness Classification rationale: Presence of fields is machine-checkable (hard), but whether values are 'actual' and 'realistic' requires engineering judgement against real-world cost/process knowledge - this is the core of what our B2 sourcing work supports. Notes: Field presence is hard-checkable; whether values are realistic requires engineering judgement - this is what B2 sourcing supports

Rule ID: S_3.5.4 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM - all parts Parameter field: bought_or_made Operator: in Limit value: {bought, made} Units: enum FSG reference: S 3.5.4, p.115 Deterministic: True Rule text: Each constituent part of an assembly must be classified as bought or made. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary field, enumerated values (bought/made) - directly machine-checkable for presence and validity.

Rule ID: S_3.5.5 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM - all parts Parameter field: part_breakdown_fields Operator: includes Limit value: {materials, processes, fasteners, tooling, overhead} Units: field_set FSG reference: S 3.5.5, p.115 Deterministic: True Rule text: Each part in the CCBOM is broken down into: materials, processes, fasteners (if applicable), tooling (if applicable), overhead. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Structural/schema requirement - checkable as a completeness test on the data model, matches our materials.csv/processes.csv/fasteners.csv schema directly. Notes: Maps directly to materials.csv/processes.csv/fasteners.csv schema

Rule ID: S_3.5.6 Source type: engineering Affected part/category: CCBOM - made parts Parameter field: part_specific_tooling_included Operator: subjective_review Limit value: N/A Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.5.6, p.115 Deterministic: False Rule text: Production tooling specific to part geometry must be included (e.g. dies to stamp a chassis bracket). Classification: engineering-soundness Classification rationale: Requires engineering judgement to determine whether a given process genuinely requires part-specific tooling versus generic tooling - not a simple lookup. Notes: Requires judging whether tooling is genuinely part-specific vs generic

Rule ID: S_3.5.7 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM - tooling costs Parameter field: tool_type Operator: not_in Limit value: {hand_tool, power_tool} Units: category FSG reference: S 3.5.7, p.115 Deterministic: True Rule text: Hand or power tools must not be included (in tooling costs). Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary exclusion rule - a tool either is or is not a hand/power tool per a defined category list.

Rule ID: S_3.5.8 Source type: engineering Affected part/category: CCBOM - bought parts Parameter field: modification_scope Operator: subjective_review Limit value: N/A Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.5.8, p.115 Deterministic: False Rule text: For bought parts, only fasteners must be included in emissions calc. Fasteners are not bought parts. If a bought part was modified, associated processes/tooling for the modification must be included. Classification: engineering-soundness Classification rationale: The 'if modified' condition requires judging whether a change to a bought part constitutes a genuine modification - not purely binary. Notes: Judging whether a change constitutes a genuine modification requires engineering judgement

Rule ID: S_3.5.9 Source type: engineering Affected part/category: CCBOM - modified bought parts Parameter field: cost_boundary_of_modification Operator: subjective_review Limit value: N/A Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.5.9, p.115 Deterministic: False Rule text: A modified bought part is a make part where the bought part acts as material. Processes/tooling/fasteners/overhead for modifications must be included; carbon footprint of the original bought part itself should not be considered. Classification: engineering-soundness Classification rationale: Correct application requires understanding the modification's scope and cost boundary - an engineering judgement call, not a lookup. Notes: Correct cost/emissions boundary for modifications requires engineering judgement

Rule ID: S_3.5.10 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM - bought parts Parameter field: catalog_availability Operator: == Limit value: true Units: boolean FSG reference: S 3.5.10, p.115 Deterministic: True Rule text: Only parts that can be bought from a catalog may be designated as bought parts. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary test in principle: does a catalog listing exist for this exact part? Directly maps to our source_register's 'is this sourced from a real supplier catalog' check. Notes: Maps to source_register: is there a real supplier catalog entry?

Rule ID: S_3.5.11 Source type: interpretive Affected part/category: CCBOM - all parts Parameter field: cost_realism_standard Operator: subjective_review Limit value: as_realistic_as_possible Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.5.11, p.115 Deterministic: False Rule text: Cost calculations must be as realistic as possible and exclude R&D and capital expenditure for real estate (plant, development hours). Classification: interpretive Classification rationale: 'As realistic as possible' is inherently a judge-scored qualitative standard, not a testable threshold. This is the exact rule that drove our B2 real-sourcing approach, since there is no official rate table to check against. Notes: Judge-scored qualitative standard, no fixed threshold - drove our B2 real-sourcing approach since no official rate table exists

Rule ID: S_3.5.12 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM - all costs Parameter field: currency Operator: == Limit value: EUR Units: currency_code FSG reference: S 3.5.12, p.115 Deterministic: True Rule text: All costs must be displayed in EUR. For non-EUR currencies, the team must provide the exchange rate used. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary/structural: currency field must equal EUR, and a documented exchange rate must be present for any conversion - directly maps to what we've been doing in materials.csv notes throughout B2. Notes: If non-EUR source used, exchange_rate_documented must also be true

Rule ID: S_3.5.13 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM - all parts Parameter field: cost_ceiling Operator: N/A Limit value: no_maximum Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.5.13, p.116 Deterministic: True Rule text: There is no maximum cost. Receipts are not required for any items. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Explicitly states the absence of a constraint - trivially satisfied, included for completeness. Notes: Trivially satisfied - no upper bound constraint exists

Rule ID: S_3.5.14 Source type: hard Affected part/category: CCBOM - process rates Parameter field: rate_calculation_shown Operator: == Limit value: true Units: boolean FSG reference: S 3.5.14, p.116 Deterministic: True Rule text: The calculations for machine hourly rates, wages (including overheads) etc. must be shown. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary presence check: is a calculation/derivation shown for each rate, or is it an unexplained number? Directly maps to our processes.csv notes column requirement. Notes: Maps to processes.csv notes column requirement

Rule ID: S_3.5.15_to_18 Source type: engineering Affected part/category: CCBOM - carbon footprint (out of scope for cost work) Parameter field: lca_methodology Operator: subjective_review Limit value: N/A Units: N/A FSG reference: S 3.5.15-3.5.18, p.116 Deterministic: False Rule text: Carbon footprint calculated as Cradle-to-Gate LCA including raw material extraction, manufacturing, transportation between steps; excludes R&D. Classification: engineering-soundness Classification rationale: LCA methodology correctness requires domain expertise to apply properly (system boundaries, emission factors) - objectively gradable by an expert but not simply machine-checkable. NOTE: out of scope for current B-stage work (cost focus, not emissions) - flagged for awareness only. Notes: LCA correctness requires domain expertise - out of scope for current cost-focused B-stages, flagged for awareness only

Rule ID: S_3.7.2 Source type: hard Affected part/category: Cost and Emissions Explanation File Parameter field: cost_model_documented Operator: == Limit value: true Units: boolean FSG reference: S 3.7.2, p.116 Deterministic: True Rule text: The cost model used must be pointed out, especially which specific costs are included (e.g. machine operation costs). Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary presence/completeness check: is the cost model methodology documented? Directly maps to our provenance_notes.md and per-row notes approach. Notes: Maps to provenance_notes.md and per-row notes approach

Rule ID: S_3.8.3 Source type: hard Affected part/category: BOM - all parts Parameter field: missing_items_count Operator: == Limit value: 0 Units: count FSG reference: S 3.8.3, p.116 Deterministic: True Rule text: If items are missing from the BOM, points are deducted until 0 points are scored for BOM Discussion. Classification: hard Classification rationale: Binary completeness check against the vehicle's actual part list, with a defined (if unspecified-magnitude) penalty function. Notes: Penalty scales with missing-item count down to 0 points

Rule ID: DERIVED_QG_001 Source type: derived_quality_gate Affected part/category: CCBOM - all parts (materials, processes, fasteners) Parameter field: source_id Operator: not_null_and_exists_in_register Limit value: N/A Units: N/A FSG reference: Deterministic: True Notes: DERIVED SOFTWARE QUALITY GATE, NOT AN FSG RULE. Every material/process/fastener cost value used by the evaluator must have a non-null source_id that exists as a row in docs/source_register.csv. This is a proxy/internal check supporting S_3.5.11 (realistic costs) but is explicitly separate from it - S_3.5.11 itself remains interpretive/non-deterministic since 'realistic' has no fixed threshold and cannot be proven by this or any other automated check. This gate only verifies traceability (a source exists), not realism/correctness of the cost value itself. Passing this check is necessary but not sufficient for S_3.5.11 compliance.

## Important: 18 deterministic, 9 non-deterministic — please route accordingly and `S_3.4.8` (part naming clarity — no ontology exists to machine-verify this). **Please don't build automated pass/fail checks for these 9** — they need to stay flagged for human/judge review, or your pipeline will produce false confidence on things that genuinely require engineering judgement. ## New: DERIVED_QG_001 — internal provenance quality gate (NOT an FSG rule) Per your request, I've added a check: **every material/process/fastener cost value used by the evaluator must have a non-null `source_id` that exists in `docs/source_register.csv`.** This is `rule_category: "derived_quality_gate"` in the dataset — deliberately **separate** from `S_3.5.11`. Important distinction: - `S_3.5.11` ("realistic costs") **stays interpretive/non-deterministic** — no fixed threshold can prove "realism," so it's not being reclassified. - `DERIVED_QG_001` only checks **traceability** (does a source exist?), not correctness or realism of the value itself. - **Passing DERIVED_QG_001 is necessary but not sufficient** for `S_3.5.11` compliance — a cost could have a valid source and still not be realistic (e.g. a wrong material grade), and this gate won't catch that. Please implement this as internal tooling/CI-style validation, not as something that appears in FSG compliance reporting

# Provenance Notes ## Purpose This document defines the conventions used in `source_register.csv` and `data/raw/` so that every value in the processed tables can be traced back to a specific, dated source. ## source_id naming convention - Official FSG documents: `FSG_<TOPIC>_<YEAR>` e.g. `FSG_RULES_2026` - Material datasheets: `MAT_<NNN>` e.g. `MAT_001` - Supplier snapshots: `SUP_<SUPPLIERNAME>_<YYYYMMDD>` e.g. `SUP_MISUMI_20260821` - Public team reports: `TEAM_<TEAMNAME_OR_ID>_<YEAR>` - Synthetic data batches: `SYN_<TOPIC>_<NNN>` IDs are permanent once assigned. Never reuse or reassign an ID, even if the source is later found to be wrong or unusable — mark it deprecated instead. ## Snapshot rule If a web source (supplier catalogue, online datasheet) changes over time, create a NEW source_id with a new date suffix. Never overwrite or edit an existing raw file. Old snapshots stay in `data/raw/` even if unused. ## Authority hierarchy (for resolving disagreements between sources) 1. Official FSG rules/cost documents (highest authority) 2. Manufacturer/material datasheets 3. Supplier catalogue/API data 4. Public team reports (treat as illustrative, not authoritative) 5. Generic catalogue / synthetic data (lowest — always flagged synthetic=true) When two sources disagree, record both

## Authority hierarchy (for resolving disagreements between sources) 3. Supplier catalogue/API data 4. Public team reports (treat as illustrative, not authoritative) 5. Generic catalogue / synthetic data (lowest — always flagged synthetic=true) When two sources disagree, record both values, cite this hierarchy to choose the one used downstream, and keep a note of the disagreement — do not silently discard the lower-authority value. ## Redistribution status Every source_id gets a `redistributable` value of one of: - `yes` — confirmed safe to include in public benchmark release - `no` — confirmed proprietary/restricted, research use only - `check` — not yet verified; default for all new entries until confirmed Nothing is marked `yes` by default. Public team reports default to `no` unless the team has given explicit permission. ## What "raw" means `data/raw/` holds original files exactly as obtained (PDF, screenshot, CSV export, HTML save).
